title: Rust: Hello, World!
description: Print output to the console using println! macro in Rust.

steps.title: Print Hello, Rust!
steps.description: Write a Rust program that prints `Hello, Rust!` to the console using the `println!` macro.
hints: Don't forget the main function: `fn main() { }`

verification.failureMessage: Make sure you print exactly 'Hello, Rust!'.

steps.title: Print with Variables
steps.description: Declare a variable `message` with value `"Rust is fun!"` using `let` and print it with `println!`.
hints: Pass the variable to `println!` with `{}` placeholder.

verification.failureMessage: Print the variable so 'Rust is fun!' appears.

steps.title: Multiple Arguments
steps.description: Use `println!` with multiple placeholders to print `"My name is Rust and I am 10 years old"`.
hints: `println!("My name is {} and I am {} years old", name, age)`
Use `{}` for each value you want to insert.

verification.failureMessage: Print 'My name is ... and I am ... years old' using println! with placeholders.

steps.title: Print with Debug Format
steps.description: Print a tuple `(1, "hello", 3.14)` using the debug formatter `{:?}` with `println!`.
hints: The `{:?}` formatter works for any type that implements the Debug trait.

verification.failureMessage: Print the tuple using {:?} format specifier.

steps.title: Print Multiple Values
steps.description: Print `"apple"`, `"banana"`, and `"cherry"` each on a separate line using three separate `println!` calls.
hints: `println!` automatically adds a newline at the end.
Write `println!("apple");` then repeat for banana and cherry.

verification.failureMessage: Print each fruit on its own line.
